name: Shorby
summary: Link-in-bio pages and short links, with messenger deep-links into WhatsApp or Telegram and retargeting pixels firing on every click.
best_for: creators and businesses that sell via messenger conversations or retarget link-in-bio traffic with ad pixels
skip_if: you just need a links page (free tools abound), or your audience doesn't click through to chat apps
honest_knock: In a category where the market leader has a generous free plan, Shorby charges from day one, so it has to earn the gap. Its case rests on two differentiated features: messenger deep-links, one tap into WhatsApp/Telegram chats, and retargeting pixels firing on every click. If you use neither, Linktree's free tier wins; if messenger-first selling or ad retargeting is your funnel, the $15 pays for itself.

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-09-25 at dash.shorby.com/pricing) Three paid plans, no free plan on the table. Rocket $15/mo, or $12/mo billed annually ($36 off the year); Pro $29/mo, or $24/mo annually ($60 off); Agency $99/mo, or $82/mo annually ($204 off). Pages included: 5 on Rocket, 50 on Pro, 250 on Agency, with Agency adding Projects and Teams from three up. Direct messenger buttons, Click Insights and Shor Rewards are on all three; Google Analytics, custom domains (per project) and Dynamic Feeds (5 per page) start at Pro. The table states all prices are in USD and all sales are final. Note that the marketing site's own /pricing/ page renders nothing — this table is only reachable at dash.shorby.com. Agency includes three projects; each further project is $12.50/mo (4th-20th), $8.33/mo (21st-100th) or $5.83/mo (101st onward), billed annually, and Agency alone lists team members (10 per project). Tracked clicks are 10k, 30k and 1M, ad-platform pixels 1, 7 and 7.

sessions.what: We built a link page on Shorby's trial on 12 November 2026, added a WhatsApp button, tried to add a second ad platform and a second project, and opened the Rocket checkout. We stopped before paying and did not publish. We did not test export, support or downgrade.
findings: The trial started without a card. The dashboard banner read 'Your trial will expire in 5 days'. The editor opened empty, and the page address returned 404 before publishing, so a draft stays private.

A WhatsApp button took about 20 seconds: a placeholder number with country code and a predefined message, then a black WhatsApp button on the page. Telegram, Messenger, Skype, Viber and e-mail are in the same list.

The pixel list offers 9 platforms. Adding a second ad platform to one pixel set (Facebook plus Google Ads, with placeholder IDs) returned 'Please upgrade your subscription plan to add more Ad platforms'. The trial allows one.
Creating a second project returned 'Please upgrade your subscription plan to add more projects'. The trial allows one project.
The pricing page preselects annual billing: Rocket $12 a month, Pro $24, Agency $82, with 'all prices in USD all sales are final'.

The Rocket checkout showed an annual saving of $36 and 'Total: $144 per year', with Stripe card fields. We saw no tax line. Stripe offered a saved payment method from the browser, which we did not click.
not_tested: Publishing the page and how the messenger button behaves on a phone
Support replies, team invitations and API access
